     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeAtBaseField
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingAffineReduction
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Etale-locality of the degree-zero condition
    11	
    12	The degree-zero condition on an affine test is reflected by restriction to a singleton
    13	faithfully flat etale cover.  Given a field point of the base, base-change the cover to that
    14	field and refine it by a finite separable field extension.  The resulting point of the cover
    15	lies above the extended base point.  Degree zero upstairs therefore descends through
    16	`degAt_overSpecMap_eq_zero_iff`.
    17	
    18	This is the degree-condition half of etale descent for `pic0`.  It does not assert effectivity
    19	of descent for the underlying `picEt` class.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    33	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    34	
    35	noncomputable section
    36	
    37	/-- If a Picard class becomes degree zero on a singleton faithfully flat etale cover of an
    38	affine test, then it was already degree zero on the base. -/
    39	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_of_etaleCover
    40	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    41	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A))
    42	    (h : picEtMap C
    43	        (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) lam
    44	      ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :
    45	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) := by
    46	  rw [mem_pic0Subgroup_iff] at h ⊢
    47	  intro K _ _ t
    48	  obtain ⟨phi, rfl⟩ := exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom (k := k) A K t
    49	  letI : Algebra A K := phi.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    50	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A K :=
    51	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (phi.commutes a).symm
    52	  let F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := E.baseChange K
    53	  obtain ⟨L, instFieldL, instAlgebraKL, instFiniteKL, instSeparableKL, ⟨j⟩⟩ :=
    54	    F.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
    55	  letI : Field L := instFieldL
    56	  letI : Algebra K L := instAlgebraKL
    57	  letI : Module.Finite K L := instFiniteKL
    58	  letI : Algebra.IsSeparable K L := instSeparableKL
    59	  letI : Algebra k L :=
    60	    ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
    61	  haveI : IsScalarTower k K L :=
    62	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    63	  let psi : E.Carrier →ₐ[k] L :=
    64	    (j.restrictScalars k).comp ((E.baseChangeInclude K).restrictScalars k)
    65	  let kappa : K →ₐ[k] L := IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K L
    66	  have hcomp :
    67	      psi.comp ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) =
    68	        kappa.comp phi := by
    69	    ext a
    70	    simp only [psi, kappa, AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.restrictScalars_apply,
    71	      Algebra.ofId_apply, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom']
    72	    rw [← j.commutes (phi a)]
    73	    apply congrArg j
    74	    apply (E.baseChangeEquiv K).injective
    75	    unfold Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeInclude
    76	    simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, AlgHom.restrictScalars_apply,
    77	      Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply]
    78	    change (E.baseChangeEquiv K)
    79	        ((E.baseChangeEquiv K).symm
    80	          (1 ⊗ₜ[A] (algebraMap A E.Carrier) a)) =
    81	      (E.baseChangeEquiv K) (algebraMap K F.Carrier (phi a))
    82	    rw [(E.baseChangeEquiv K).apply_symm_apply,
    83	      (E.baseChangeEquiv K).commutes,
    84	      Algebra.TensorProduct.algebraMap_apply]
    85	    convert (TensorProduct.smul_tmul (R := A) a
    86	      (1 : K) (1 : E.Carrier)).symm using 1 <;>
    87	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one,
    88	        RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, RingHom.id_apply]
    89	    exact congrArg (fun x : K => x ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : E.Carrier))
    90	      (congrFun (AlgHom.coe_toRingHom phi) a).symm
    91	  have hzero :
    92	      degAt lam
    93	        (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫
    94	          Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) = 0 := by
    95	    rw [← degAt_picEtMap]
    96	    exact h L (Over.overSpecMap psi)
    97	  have hpoint :
    98	      Over.overSpecMap kappa ≫ Over.overSpecMap phi =
    99	        Over.overSpecMap psi ≫
   100	          Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) := by
   101	    rw [← Over.overSpecMap_comp, ← Over.overSpecMap_comp, hcomp]
   102	  rw [← hpoint] at hzero
   103	  exact (degAt_overSpecMap_eq_zero_iff lam kappa (Over.overSpecMap phi)).mp hzero
   104	
   105	end
   106	
   107	end AlgebraicGeometry

A class over the carrier of a singleton etale cover whose two restrictions to the
double overlap agree descends to the base.  The representative cover is composed with
the given cover.  Its raw relative-Picard descent condition is checked after restriction
to a cover of the double overlap and reflected by etale separatedness.

`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:

```bash
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
```

### 2a. THE RELEASE IS AS DANGEROUS AS THE REAP — check the pidfile before `rm -rf` (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The acquire loop above is careful; the release (`rm -rf "$LOCK"`) is not, and that asymmetry
caused a real incident. **A lane removed the lock directory while its pidfile named a LIVE pid
belonging to another lane's build**, having printed `ALIVE` for that pid one line earlier.

The mechanism is worth stating because nothing in the recipe warns about it. The offending lane
had legitimately acquired the lock, and then **its own shell was killed by a harness timeout
while it held it**. On the next turn it reasoned "the lock is mine and my holder is dead, so
release it" — but in the interval a *different* lane had acquired the lock, so the pid in the
file had never been its own. The lane was running the release branch on a belief about history
rather than on a reading of the file.

> **Before `rm -rf "$LOCK"`, verify the pidfile still names YOUR pid.**
> `[ "$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -rf "$LOCK"`
> If it names anything else, the lock is not yours to release: say so and leave it alone.

* **"It was mine a minute ago" is not evidence**, especially when a harness can kill the shell

data.command:
/bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
review_lock=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
review_acquired=0
for review_attempt in $(seq 1 24)
do
  if mkdir "$review_lock" 2>/dev/null
  then
    review_acquired=1
    break
  fi
  review_holder=unknown
  if [ -f "$review_lock/pid" ]
  then
    review_holder=$(sed -n '"'1p' \""'$review_lock/pid")
  fi
  printf '"'waiting for AJCR Lake mutex held by %s\\n' \""'$review_holder"
  sleep 5
done
if [ "$review_acquired" -ne 1 ]
then
  printf '"'could not acquire AJCR Lake mutex\\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
review_owner="'$$
printf '"'%s\\n' \""'$review_owner" > "$review_lock/pid"
review_cleanup() {
  if [ -f "$review_lock/pid" ] && [ "$(sed -n '"'1p' \""'$review_lock/pid")" = "$review_owner" ]
  then
    unlink "$review_lock/pid"
    rmdir "$review_lock"
  fi
}
trap review_cleanup EXIT
lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffEtaleEffectivity
lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0EtaleDegreeZero'

1	/-
     2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors. All rights reserved.
     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffEtaleEffectivity
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0EtaleDegreeZero
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveSite
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# Affine etale descent for Pic0
    12	
    13	Compatible degree-zero Picard data over a singleton faithfully flat etale cover descend
    14	uniquely to the affine base.  Existence first descends the underlying `PicEtAff` class, then
    15	reflects the fibrewise degree-zero condition through the cover.  Uniqueness is affine
    16	`PicEtAff` etale separatedness.
    17	
    18	This is the affine algebraic input for the big-etale sheaf comparison.  It does not assert a
    19	Scheme-site sheaf certificate or identify the raw functor with its sheafification.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	
    28	open scoped TensorProduct
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-- Compatible degree-zero Picard data over a singleton faithfully flat etale cover have a
    35	unique degree-zero descent to the affine base. -/
    36	theorem pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_etaleCover
    37	    {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    38	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    39	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	    [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    41	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
    42	    (x : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k E.Carrier))
    43	    (h : pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInl E)) x =
    44	      pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInr E)) x) :
    45	    ∃! z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A),
    46	      pic0Map C
    47	        (Over.overSpecMap
    48	          ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) z = x := by
    49	  let phi : A →ₐ[k] E.Carrier :=
    50	    (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k
    51	  have hPic :
    52	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInl E))
    53	          (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
    54	        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInr E))
    55	          (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
    56	    exact congrArg Subtype.val h
    57	  have hAff :
    58	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C (doubleInl E)
    59	          (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
    60	            (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) =
    61	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C (doubleInr E)
    62	          (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
    63	            (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) := by
    64	    rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, ← picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
    65	    exact congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier)) hPic
    66	  obtain ⟨zAff, hzAff⟩ :=
    67	    PicEtAff.exists_map_eq_of_double_eq C E
    68	      (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
    69	        (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) hAff
    70	  let zPic : picEt C (overSpec k A) :=
    71	    (picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm zAff
    72	  have hzPic :
    73	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi) zPic =
    74	        (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
    75	    apply (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier).injective
    76	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
    77	    simp only [zPic, MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    78	    rw [PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl]
    79	    exact hzAff
    80	  have hzMem : zPic ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) :=
    81	    mem_pic0Subgroup_of_etaleCover E zPic (by
    82	      rw [hzPic]
    83	      exact x.2)
    84	  let z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) := ⟨zPic, hzMem⟩
    85	  have hz :
    86	      pic0Map C
    87	        (Over.overSpecMap
    88	          ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) z = x :=
    89	    Subtype.ext hzPic
    90	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
    91	  intro y hy
    92	  apply Subtype.ext
    93	  apply (picEtAffineEquiv C A).injective
    94	  apply PicEtAff.map_injective_of_etaleCover C E
    95	  have hyz := hy.trans hz.symm
    96	  have hyPic :
    97	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi)
    98	          (y : picEt C (overSpec k A)) =
    99	        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi)
   100	          (z : picEt C (overSpec k A)) := by
   101	    exact congrArg Subtype.val hyz
   102	  have hyAff := congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier) hyPic
   103	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, picEtAffineEquiv_naturality,
   104	    PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl,
   105	    PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl] at hyAff
   106	  exact hyAff
   107	
   108	end
   109	
   110	end AlgebraicGeometry

    \""'$git_tool" commit-tree "$tree" -p "$old")

    printf '"'commit=%s\\nparent=%s\\n' \""'$new" "$old"

    "$git_tool" diff "$old" "$new" -- "$rootpath"
    exit 0
  fi
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
done

      "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffEtaleEffectivity
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0EtaleDegreeZero
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveSite

/-!
# Affine etale descent for Pic0

Compatible degree-zero Picard data over a singleton faithfully flat etale cover descend
uniquely to the affine base.  Existence first descends the underlying `PicEtAff` class, then
reflects the fibrewise degree-zero condition through the cover.  Uniqueness is affine
`PicEtAff` etale separatedness.

This is the affine algebraic input for the big-etale sheaf comparison.  It does not assert a
Scheme-site sheaf certificate or identify the raw functor with its sheafification.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Compatible degree-zero Picard data over a singleton faithfully flat etale cover have a
unique degree-zero descent to the affine base. -/
theorem pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_etaleCover
    {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
    (x : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k E.Carrier))
    (h : pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInl E)) x =
      pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInr E)) x) :
    ∃! z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A),
      pic0Map C
        (Over.overSpecMap
          ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) z = x := by
  let phi : A →ₐ[k] E.Carrier :=
    (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k
  have hPic :
      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInl E))
          (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInr E))
          (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
    exact congrArg Subtype.val h
  have hAff :
      PicEtAff.mapAlg C (doubleInl E)
          (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
            (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) =
        PicEtAff.mapAlg C (doubleInr E)
          (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
            (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) := by
    rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, ← picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
    exact congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier)) hPic
  obtain ⟨zAff, hzAff⟩ :=
    PicEtAff.exists_map_eq_of_double_eq C E
      (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
        (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) hAff
  let zPic : picEt C (overSpec k A) :=
    (picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm zAff
  have hzPic :
      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi) zPic =
        (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
    apply (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier).injective
    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
    simp only [zPic, MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    rw [PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl]
    exact hzAff
  have hzMem : zPic ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) :=
    mem_pic0Subgroup_of_etaleCover E zPic (by
      rw [hzPic]
      exact x.2)
  let z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) := ⟨zPic, hzMem⟩
  have hz :
      pic0Map C
        (Over.overSpecMap
          ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) z = x :=
    Subtype.ext hzPic
  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
  intro y hy
  apply Subtype.ext
  apply (picEtAffineEquiv C A).injective
  apply PicEtAff.map_injective_of_etaleCover C E
  have hyz := hy.trans hz.symm
  have hyPic :
      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi)
          (y : picEt C (overSpec k A)) =
        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi)
          (z : picEt C (overSpec k A)) := by
    exact congrArg Subtype.val hyz
  have hyAff := congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier) hyPic
  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, picEtAffineEquiv_naturality,
    PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl,
    PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl] at hyAff
  exact hyAff

end

end AlgebraicGeometry
